title: Why Finance "Gurus" Want You To Hate Them - How Money Works
summary: Explainer on why finance gurus act obnoxious: controversy gives free reach, filters for impressionable buyers, and a personal brand lets them sell any trending scheme.

assertions.quote: these people will present themselves as wildly successful before offering up the secrets to their success for a steep price
only to be taught big self-help nonsense rather than practical sales advice
converting just one percent of 5 million viewers is better than converting 50 of 10 000 viewers and it's free

verdicts.note: Plausible funnel economics; the motive is inferred.

assertions.quote: they don't want to waste their time dealing with people who are smart enough to read

verdicts.note: The typo-filter hypothesis for scam email has research support; the extension to gurus is inference.

assertions.quote: they can slap their brand on whatever is popular at the time
the courses these guys sell don't instantly turn average joes into jordan belfort's over the course of a five day seminar

verdicts.note: Sales performance develops over years of practice; no short course has demonstrated otherwise.

assertions.quote: a good salesman can easily make more than almost any other employee because their income is determined by performance-based commissions

verdicts.note: Top salespeople earn highly, but median sales pay is ordinary and variable.
Top commissioned salespeople out-earn most employees, but median sales pay is ordinary and the 'can' only holds for the high performers.
